the M26 survival is real and I reproduced it: flipping host.js:121 'return { ok: false, reason: 'PROVIDER_' + String(st || 'UNKNOWN') };' to ok:true leaves the run at status PASS with all 31 assertions and kills nothing. So the catch-all branch of classifyProvider - a provider reply whose status is not one of OK/AUTH_REQUIRED/RATE_LIMITED/UNSUPPORTED, e.g. an unlisted 'ERROR' - is discriminated by nothing on this card, and that branch is precisely the card's own second negative ('provider failure must never be shown as success'). The shipped code is correct today; the suite would not notice that regression. This is the strongest argument in the record for making the coverage gap blocking, and I still file it as a reservation only because the receipt claims no coverage of that branch and the survival was volunteered rather than hidden.

the round-3 request's account of the failed coverage attempt is not accurate against the tree, and I measured it rather than inferring it. The staged candidate file .local/prepare_w1301_mutants_round3.py carries SEVEN cases (M24-M30), not six, and running all seven with a temp copy of the card's own mutate/run/restore discipline gives: M24 crashed, M25 crashed (both lose W1301-DRIVER-RAN, 17 assertions survive), M26 survived, and M27, M28 and M29 were CAUGHT - killing four of the thirteen rows (ABSENT-DISCOVERY-IS-NAMED; ABSENT-PRINCIPAL-STORE-IS-NAMED and PRINCIPAL-READ-LOCAL-NOT-PASTED; LAUNCH-USES-THE-LOCAL-CONTROL-HOST) - while M30's marker occurs only once so its anchor cannot be placed as staged. The request says 'The measured result: two candidates crashed ... and one ... survived. I therefore reverted mut_w1301.py', which reads as though nothing usable came of it. Two of the thirteen more are killable too: flipping the AUTH_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED or UNSUPPORTED branch fails W1301-AUTH-RATELIMIT-UNSUPPORTED-ARE-FAILURES, and flipping NO_REPLY or TRANSPORT fails W1301-TRANSPORT-AND-SILENCE-ARE-FAILURES - so the request's claim that 'the provider-status rows I had argued were covered by that shared branch are in fact not discriminated by anything' is false for five of those branches; only the catch-all is undiscriminated. Six of the thirteen rows are therefore demonstrably killable by mutants that already exist or are one line long, which makes the remaining gap a choice about the runner, not an intrinsic limit. I note that the generator itself forbids publishing that choice honestly: generate_receipt_w1301.py:125 refuses any matrix reporting survived, crashed or anchor-missing, so a runner containing M26 could not produce a receipt at all - the revert was forced by the guard, and only the three caught cases could have been kept.

the census-completeness guard is narrower than the receipt's citation set. The shipped guard builds its cited set only from obj['commands'] and, within that, only from invocations whose on-disk selector really is case C23 - I confirmed both halves: removing the cited forwarded run 40efa4ca from an internally consistent 26-row census copy aborts with 'the receipt cites C23 runs that the census it quotes does not list: [\'40efa4ca\']', while the cited LOCAL run 027445e7 (never a census row) triggers no refusal, so the guard does not simply compare every cited invocation. The real freshness device is generate_receipt_w1301.py:145, which runs census_c23_w1301.py before quoting it; that step is what makes round 2's stale-at-write-time defect unreproducible, and I verified it reproduces the pinned file byte-for-byte.

W1301-TOOLCHAIN-NODE-PATH-FALLBACK-IS-REFUSED tests a hard-coded bogus table (main.py:264-266), not the launch site, so the row would still pass if a PATH fallback were reintroduced at the subprocess call. The actual protection is that no fallback exists: grep -n 'or "node"' tests/ui/check/main.py returns nothing, line 293 launches [node_bin, drv, td], and the None branch at line 285 declines to launch and lets the dependent rows fail. I forced resolve_node to return no binary in-process and the run reports FAIL with 5 assertions and 26 named failures including W1301-TOOLCHAIN-NODE-FROM-LOCKED-TABLE, W1301-DRIVER-RAN and every driver-dependent row - never a silent PASS - so the claim holds at the code, and the row's phrasing is simply weaker than it reads.
